newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian sobs as charged with Briton's murder.
newsitem.headline: Australian sobs as charged with Briton's murder.

text.p: A 22-year-old unemployed Australian man sobbed in a Sydney court on Tuesday as he was charged with beating to death British tourist Brian Hagland at Bondi Beach 10 days ago.
In a brief appearance in the Waverley Magistrates Court, Aaron Martin was charged with one count of murder and remanded in custody to appear again in court on November 1.
Martin's lawyer, Leigh Johnson, did not not seek bail and no plea was entered. Johnson has previously said Martin will plead not guilty.
Hagland, 28, died from head and internal injuries after being assaulted in a street attack witnessed by his fiancee in the early hours of Saturday, September 7.
Hagland's fiancee, Connie Casey, 25, has said two men kicked and punched the London postman to death in an unprovoked attack near Sydney's most famous beach.
Martin voluntarily walked into the Bondi Beach police station last week to assist police with their investigation. When he returned for a second interview on Monday, he was arrested.
During Tuesday's court hearing, Martin, who was dressed in a grey suit and black tie, covered his face and sobbed.
Outside court, police said investigations into Hagland's death were continuing. The prosecutor told the court that it would take a month to prepare the case, which would involve 34 witnesses.
Sitting in court was Martin's mother, Jan, who collapsed as she left court, falling down 10 stairs. When she came to, she too began to cry. "My son is not a murderer," she said.
Casey and Hagland had been in Australia for eight months and had been due to visit New Zealand before returning to Britain to be married.
